label: prop:t-beta-markov-frobenius-collapse-general
title: Min-Frobenius-norm collapse: T_β = S · 1_A — general unital R-algebra lift of [prop:t-beta-markov-frobenius-collapse]
html:
Proposition. Min-Frobenius-norm collapse: T_β = S · 1_A — general unital R-algebra lift of [prop:t-beta-markov-frobenius-collapse]

Let R be a strict-ordered field. Let A be a unital R-algebra. Let \tau : A \to R be an R-linear normalised trace (\tau(1) = 1, \tau(xy) = \tau(yx)). Assume \tau is positive-semi-definite on squares: 0 \le \tau(X \cdot X) for all X \in A. For any S \in R and X \in A satisfying \tau(X) = S, we have:

S^2 \;\le\; \tau(X \cdot X).

If \tau is non-degenerate on squares (\tau(Y \cdot Y) = 0 \implies Y = 0), the lower bound is attained if and only if X = S \cdot 1_A.

Relation to the substrate-model version

This proposition lifts prop:t-beta-markov-frobenius-collapse from the substrate model (A = R, \tau = \mathrm{id}) to the general unital R-algebra setting, where A may be non-commutative and infinite-dimensional.

Application to the Iwahori–Hecke algebra

For A = H_n(R, q) at generic q > 0 with \tau = \mathrm{tr}_M, this proposition identifies the canonical SDP-min-Frobenius-norm operator for the constraint \mathrm{tr}_M(T_\beta) = S:

T_\beta^{\mathrm{Markov}} \;=\; S \cdot 1_H.

The L^2-Euclidean coordinate-norm operator and the Markov-Frobenius operator both reproduce the SDP constraint. The observable c_k Taylor coefficients remain invariant.
